# Dependabot runbook

How dependency updates arrive in this repo, what each badge means, and the
one-pass routine for the grouped patch PR.

## Review tiers

| Badge in title | Label | What it is | Routine |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[✅ PATCH-ONLY]` | `deps: patch ✅ one-pass review` | **One** grouped PR with every patch-level bump across all packages (`Bump the patch-only-safe group across N directories with M updates`). | CI green → lockfiles-only diff → merge. One pass. |
| `[🟡 MINOR]` | `deps: minor 🟡` | Individual PR, minor bump, one dependency in one package. | Read release notes, CI green, smoke-test if UI-facing. |
| `[🔴 MAJOR]` | `deps: major 🔴 breaking-risk` | Individual PR, major bump. | Migration guide, cross-repo impact, manual regression. Or `@dependabot ignore this major version`. |
| `[🔒 SECURITY]` | `deps: security 🔒` | **One** grouped PR for Dependabot security updates (`security-fixes` group). | Priority over everything else. CI green → merge. |

Every Dependabot PR also gets a sticky comment with a shields badge, the
metadata (highest bump, group, directories, dependencies) and the checklist for
its tier. The comment is refreshed on every rebase; the PR body is left alone
because PR-Agent rewrites it.

## Where things live

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.github/dependabot.yml` | Schedule, grouping, cooldown, policy-frozen ignores. |
| `.github/workflows/dependabot-triage.yml` | Labels, title badges, sticky comment, opt-in auto-merge. |
| `CODEOWNERS` | Reviewer assignment. The old `reviewers:` key in `dependabot.yml` was removed by GitHub in May 2025. |

## First-time setup (once, by a repo admin)

1. Merge the two files to `develop` (the default branch; Dependabot reads the
   config from there).
2. Actions → **Dependabot Triage** → **Run workflow**. This creates the four
   tier labels. Dependabot never creates custom labels itself.
3. Settings → Code security → confirm **Dependabot alerts** and
   **Dependabot security updates** are enabled. Leave **Grouped security
   updates** as is: the `security-fixes` group in the config overrides it.
4. Optional, for hands-off patch merging:
   - Settings → General → enable **Allow auto-merge**.
   - Branch protection on `develop` with the three CI suites as required checks.
   - Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → **Variables** → add
     `DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_PATCH` = `true`.
   Until that variable exists, nothing merges on its own.

## Weekly cadence

Thursday 09:00 IST for npm, docker and GitHub Actions. Dependabot opens the
patch group plus up to nine individual minor/major PRs per run (limit 10 open).

To refresh on demand: **Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot → Check for
updates** (per ecosystem). Config errors show on the same page.

## Cooldown (supply-chain guard)

A release is not proposed until it has been public for:

| Bump | Days |
|---|---|
| patch | 7 |
| minor | 14 |
| major | 30 |

Security updates ignore cooldown. Lower the numbers in `dependabot.yml` if a
needed fix is being held back.

## Policy-frozen dependencies

These never get a major PR (and React never gets a minor), by design. See the
`ignore:` block in `dependabot.yml`; the reasons trace back to the Hard
Constraints in `CLAUDE.md`.

- Runtime/mesh: `react`, `react-dom`, `single-spa*`, `webpack*`, `typescript`, `sass*`
- Intentional drift: `jest*`, `eslint*`, `i18next`, `react-i18next`, `prettier`
- Shared-bundle weight: `@aot-technologies/formio*`, `@mui/*`, `bpmn-js`, `bootstrap`, `react-bootstrap`, `react-router-dom`, `keycloak-js`, `@reduxjs/toolkit`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `storybook*`

To plan one of these upgrades, delete its `ignore` entry in a feature branch
and run **Check for updates**; the PR arrives as `[🔴 MAJOR]`.

## Useful PR commands

Comment on the PR:

```text
@dependabot rebase
@dependabot recreate
@dependabot ignore this minor version
@dependabot ignore this major version
@dependabot ignore this dependency
@dependabot close
```

`recreate` is the fix when a group PR has drifted after other merges.

## Gotchas

- **Target branch.** Do not add `target-branch:` to the npm block. Security
  updates only ever target the default branch, and a non-default
  `target-branch` detaches them from the groups and labels (this is why the
  sibling `forms-flow-ai` repo still receives one-off security PRs).
- **Labels.** Unknown labels in `dependabot.yml` are silently ignored. Keep
  custom labels in the triage workflow, which creates them.
- **Secrets.** Dependabot-triggered workflow runs cannot read Actions secrets.
  The triage workflow uses only `GITHUB_TOKEN`; keep it that way.
- **Grouped PR title.** The title is generated by Dependabot and can be
  regenerated on `recreate`; the triage workflow re-applies the badge on every
  `synchronize` event.
- **`group-by: dependency-name`.** Would collapse "same dependency, five
  packages" minor bumps into one PR, but combining it with `update-types` is
  not documented. Left as a commented option in `dependabot.yml`; trial it on
  a branch before adopting.
